LESSON: VULCANICITY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GEOGRAPHY
Strand: Natural Systems and Processes
Topic 2.3: Vulcanicity
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 13

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Vulcanicity, part of Natural Systems and Processes in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GEOGRAPHY.

Key inquiry question: Why study Vulcanicity?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Brainstorm on the meaning and causes of Vulcanicity on Earth and make notes, Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC or be allowed extra time to express their views

2. Use print or digital resources to research on features resulting from Vulcanicity in the world and make presentations in class, learners using print media could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive technology. Those with manipulation difficulties could be provided with adapted digital resources or be supported to make presentations,

3. Draw the intrusive features resulting from Vulcanicity in the world and display in class.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Brainstorm on the meaning and causes of Vulcanicity on Earth and make notes, Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC or be allowed extra time to express their views
2. Use print or digital resources to research on features resulting from Vulcanicity in the world and make presentations in class, learners using print media could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive technology. Those with manipulation difficulties could be provided with adapted digital resources or be supported to make presentations,
3. Draw the intrusive features resulting from Vulcanicity in the world and display in class.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Vulcanicity together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-Efficacy: The skill of self-awareness as the learner creates a poster of volcanic features and displays in the

school compound

● Learning to Learn: The skill of working collaboratively as the learner simulates the eruption of volcanic

features

● Digital Literacy: The skill of interacting with digital technology as the learner uses digital resources to research

on features resulting from vulcanicity in the world

● Creativity and Imagination: The skill of creativity and imagination is enhanced as learners make collages on

distribution of volcanic features in the world and display in class.

● Communication and Collaboration: The skill of teamwork is enhanced as learners brainstorm, in pairs, the

meaning and causes of Vulcanicity on Earth and make notes.

Values:
● Peace: Learner exhibits tolerance as they make collage on the distribution of volcanic features in the world

● Integrity: Learner portrays self-discipline as they use digital resources to research on features resulting from

vulcanicity in the world

37

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental Education: Learner creates a poster of volcanic features and display in the school compound

● Creative Thinking: Learner makes a collage on the distribution of volcanic features in the world
